notes.title: Airline reservation changes: confirmation and baggage constraints
notes.body:
In a past airline-support interaction, the user supplied both user ID and reservation ID; reservation details were retrieved before modifying anything. For a requested one-stop-to-nonstop change, a direct-flight search was made for the outbound date/origin/destination, economy options and times were presented, and the user chose one. Before update, the agent retrieved user payment profile and explicitly restated the changed outbound, unchanged return, cabin, passenger count, and saved payment method, then asked for confirmation. The user confirmed; the flight-update tool succeeded. The user additionally asked to remove a checked bag and refund it; the agent did not attempt a baggage update and stated removal/refund could not be processed. Policy in that task says bags can be added but not removed.

Reusable ordered procedure, subject to the active policy/tools: (1) obtain user ID and reservation ID, retrieve reservation, and verify requested modification is allowed (including cabin restrictions, flown segments, and invariant trip details); (2) search viable replacement flights for applicable segment/date and cabin, present options and identify segments to remain unchanged; (3) if flight changes require a saved single gift card or credit card, verify it in the user profile; (4) summarize the complete intended change and payment method and obtain explicit confirmation before any database update; (5) update only after confirmation, then report the tool outcome; (6) handle additional requests separately against policy, declining unsupported/prohibited changes without attempting an update. Stop before a database write if confirmation or required information is absent, or policy prohibits the requested change.

Caveats: tool search output had null dates although the query specified the date; the response treated options as for the queried date, but this date behavior was not independently verified. The update response showed a -$414 payment-history entry for a two-passenger flight change, but the transcript did not explain the calculation; do not generalize the amount. No separate evaluation feedback was provided.

(2) Retrieve reservation details and verify it belongs to the user, identifying cabin, route, trip type, segments, and dates. (3) Check whether the requested change is allowed before searching or updating flights; basic economy flight changes are prohibited, while cabin changes have separate rules. (4) If the requested action is prohibited or cannot be handled within scope, do not attempt a database update; transfer to a human agent, then send the exact prescribed transfer message. (5) For an allowed update, confirm all action details and get explicit yes before changing the booking. Avoid inferring an exception from the reason for travel; the policy given here states no such exception.

notes.title: Flight booking workflow observations
notes.body:
In one airline-booking experience (no separate evaluation feedback was provided), the agent looked up the user and existing reservation, used saved passenger information after the user identified that passenger, confirmed trip details, searched availability, presented price/payment split and all booking particulars, obtained explicit go-ahead, then called the booking tool. The returned record supplied reservation ID HATHAT and matching itinerary/payment details, but its `status` field was null; the final message called the booking confirmed, so treat that confirmation as based on the returned booking record rather than an explicit status value.

For similar booking tasks: (1) obtain user ID, then retrieve profile and, if needed, reservation details; (2) establish trip type, route, cabin, passenger names and DOB, insurance choice, baggage choice, and any unclear details—use saved passenger info only when clearly identified/authorized, and avoid unnecessary re-asking of already established details; (3) search current availability and validate matching segments, dates, cabin seat counts and fares, remembering basic economy differs from economy; (4) apply baggage allowance based on booking user's membership and do not add unwanted bags; (5) ensure chosen payment methods are in profile, respect method-count limits, and verify split sums to total; (6) present complete booking summary and wait for explicit confirmation before the update call; (7) inspect the tool result and report only what it establishes, noting ambiguity such as a null status rather than inferring more. Stop and ask for missing required information or confirmation instead of booking.

For cancellation, obtain user ID, reservation ID, and reason; inspect reservation and verify eligibility before cancellation tool call (e.g. within 24 hours, airline cancellation, business cabin, or qualifying insurance/reason; check flown segments and transfer if policy requires). A reservation made May 1, evaluated May 15, economy without insurance, for 'other' reason did not meet stated criteria. For passenger changes, policy disallows changing passenger count, including via human agent; explain this clearly. Past tool results / date availability and reservation ID formatting can be surprising, so report only confirmed results and stop to ask/clarify if essential facts are missing.

notes.title: Airline reservation lookup and basic-economy change lesson
notes.body: In a past airline-support interaction, the user lacked a reservation ID but supplied their user ID and described a return-flight change to Texas. Looking up the profile’s reservations identified a Texas round trip; its basic-economy cabin meant changing its flights was outside the agent’s permitted scope, so transfer to a human was used. No separate evaluation feedback was provided, so this is an observation rather than confirmation of correctness. Applicable when a user lacks a reservation ID and requests flight changes: verify the matching itinerary and cabin before acting; do not attempt basic-economy flight changes, and transfer if the requested change cannot be handled. Avoid treating the record as proof of any broader transfer rule.

notes.title: Airline reservation lookup and basic-economy modification workflow
notes.body: In the reviewed airline interaction, the user supplied their user ID but not reservation ID and asked to change the return leg of a Texas trip. Agent retrieved the profile, checked the listed reservations, identified the matching future Texas round trip (EWR–IAH–EWR), and found it was basic economy. Under the provided policy, basic economy flights cannot be modified; transfer to a human agent was appropriate, using the required transfer tool followed by the exact hold message. No evaluation feedback was provided, so correctness is not independently verified. For similar work: (1) obtain user ID; (2) if reservation ID is missing, retrieve the user's reservations and inspect them to identify the trip matching the stated route/date/trip type; if ambiguous, ask for clarification rather than guess; (3) verify cabin and flight status/rules relevant to the requested change; (4) if modification is allowed, gather the intended changes, ensure route/destination/trip type constraints and required payment details apply, state action details and obtain explicit yes before any database update; (5) if policy makes the request out of scope (such as modifying a basic-economy flight), stop and transfer, then send the mandated transfer message. Avoid disclosing unrelated profile/reservation details.

notes.title: Airline interaction: destination-change request and handoff
notes.body: In a past airline-support interaction, user Raj Brown (user ID raj_brown_5782) asked to change reservation VA5SGQ from a DTW–LGA round trip with PHX connections to nonstop DTW–JFK flights on the same dates, Economy. Reservation lookup returned Economy; outbound date 2024-05-17, return segments dated 2024-05-19 and 2024-05-20; insurance field was "yes". User mentioned health issues and insurance and sought a supervisor/human review. The agent stated the modification rules prohibit changing origin, destination, or trip type, then successfully transferred the request to a human agent. No evaluation feedback was supplied (level: none). This record does not establish whether the agent's other assertions or handling were graded correct; no fee-waiver determination or final resolution was shown.

notes.title: Airline change request with destination change and escalation
notes.body: Past public experience (airline policy context; no evaluation feedback was provided): For a user requesting to change an existing round trip from DTW–LGA to DTW–JFK, with dates unchanged and Economy (not Basic Economy), the agent first requested user and reservation IDs, then retrieved the reservation. Details returned showed Economy, DTW–LGA via PHX, outbound May 17, 2024 and return segments May 19–20, with insurance recorded. The agent stated the change-flight rule requires retaining original origin, destination, and trip type, so it declined the LGA-to-JFK destination change and offered to search nonstop DTW–LGA on the existing dates. When the user reiterated JFK and asked if another type of modification could do it, the agent said no and mentioned separate booking as an option. When the user requested supervisor/human review, the agent transferred with a summary and sent the required transfer notice. The user’s health/insurance mention did not establish a change-fee waiver; no fee or waiver was confirmed. Do not infer whether human review would authorize an exception. Ordered procedure for similar policy-bound requests: (1) Obtain both user ID and reservation ID before reviewing/modifying; if reservation ID is unknown, use available lookup tools. (2) Retrieve and check the itinerary, cabin, trip type, and whether any segments have already been flown; distinguish Economy from Basic Economy. (3) For flight changes, verify proposed itinerary preserves origin, destination, and trip type; if it would not, stop—do not call a flight-change API or imply another modification can bypass the rule. (4) If a compliant alternative exists, offer it conditionally and search only if tools support it; do not make a booking/update without listing action details and obtaining explicit yes. (5) Do not promise a fee waiver based only on insurance or health circumstances; state only what policy/tools establish. (6) If the user explicitly seeks a human review and the request cannot be handled within agent scope, transfer using the required tool, then send the exact transfer notice. Preserve uncertainty: no human outcome or fee waiver was observed.

notes.title: Airline modification: preserve route constraints and escalate exceptions
notes.body: In a prior airline-support interaction, policy stated flight changes could not alter origin, destination, or trip type; traveler asked to change a DTW–LGA round trip to JFK, and the assistant declined that route change and transferred to a human after the user requested supervisor review. Lesson/caution: insurance and health issues do not themselves authorize a flight-change fee waiver or an exception to modification rules; when a requested exception cannot be handled within the agent's scope and a human review is requested, transfer rather than promising an outcome. Preserve uncertainty: no human-agent decision or fee-waiver outcome was provided, so do not treat the transfer as confirmation that an exception is possible or impossible.
